extracted.intended_audience: general public, media, state and federal officials, and stakeholders concerned with the FCC notice-and-comment process
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and expectations for preserving the integrity of administrative notice-and-comment rulemaking, illustrated by the Attorney General's investigation into fraudulent and identity-misused public comments submitted to the FCC. Emphasizes authenticity of comments, agency cooperation with law enforcement, and intergovernmental coordination to prevent subversion of rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment process must enable voices of affected individuals and businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal law requires the FCC and all federal agencies to take public comments on proposed rules into account — so it is important that the public comment process actually enable the voices of the millions of individuals and businesses who will be affected to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle applies across rulemaking topics (net neutrality, environmental rules, etc.). The release emphasizes that representativeness and the ability of real stakeholders to be heard is a core normative requirement of notice-and-comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments must be authentic and not fabricated or submitted using others' identities
rubrics_metrics.description: The FCC’s public comment process was being corrupted by the submission of enormous numbers of fake comments; while some fake comments used made up names and addresses, many misused the real names and addresses of actual people as part of the effort to undermine the integrity of the comment process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misuse of real names/addresses is characterized as akin to identity theft; authenticity and verified identity (or at least protections against impersonation) are necessary to preserve the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies must preserve and provide logs/records necessary for law enforcement investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General requested certain records related to the FCC's public comment system — specifically logs and other records necessary to investigate which bad actor(s) were behind the misconduct — but received no substantive response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for records were made repeatedly (at least nine times over five months); timely preservation and production of such system logs is presented as vital to investigate large-scale abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should respond substantively and timely to investigative requests from law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General's office reached out for assistance to multiple top FCC officials, including the Chairman, successive acting General Counsels, and the FCC's Inspector General, but has received no substantive response to its investigative requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive, timely cooperation (not silence) from the agency operating the targeted system is framed as necessary for successful investigation and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misuse of identities online constitutes illegal conduct warranting investigation and potential prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Impersonation and other misuse of a person’s identity violates New York law, so the Attorney General’s office launched an investigation; 'hundreds of thousands of Americans likely were victimized... That’s akin to identity theft.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement urges accountability and prosecution where appropriate, warning that failure to investigate/prosecute leaves the process open to repeated abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government levels should cooperate to stop malevolent actors subverting administrative decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: In an era where foreign governments have tried to use the internet and social media to influence our elections, federal and state governments should be working together to ensure that malevolent actors cannot subvert our administrative agencies’ decision-making processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocates intergovernmental coordination (state and federal) as a standard to defend the integrity of rulemaking against large-scale, potentially foreign-instigated manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should permit confidential sharing of records with law enforcement when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General offered to keep the requested records confidential, as his office had done previously when sharing information and documents with the FCC as part of past investigative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality assurances are presented as a practical mechanism to facilitate sharing of sensitive logs/records needed for investigations while protecting privacy or investigative integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment systems should be monitored and analyzed to detect large-scale fraudulent campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers and reporters discovered fake comments; the Attorney General’s office analyzed the fake comments and found that tens of thousands of New Yorkers — and hundreds of thousands of Americans — may have had their identities misused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active analysis and auditing of comment submissions (by researchers, reporters, and officials) is implied as necessary to detect and quantify misuse and to trigger investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking processes must be protected from coordinated efforts to 'drown out' real views
rubrics_metrics.description: Perpetrators attempted to drown out and negate the views of the real people, businesses, and others who honestly commented on this important issue; such conduct attacks what is supposed to be an open public process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensuring that aggregate comment volume reflects genuine participation rather than orchestrated fraudulent surges is a quality criterion for legitimate notice-and-comment outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity protections for public comments apply irrespective of policy position or jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Misuse of identity online by the hundreds of thousands should concern everyone — for and against net neutrality, New Yorker or Texan, Democrat or Republican.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standard is presented as neutral and universal: protecting comment integrity is an institutional requirement irrespective of the substantive positions represented or the geographic/political identity of commenters.
